name: be: am / is / are
description: The verb be in the present: I am, you are, he/she/it is, we/they are.

name: be: negative
description: Add not after am/is/are; the short forms are isn't and aren't.

name: be: questions
description: Put am/is/are before the subject; short answers repeat be (Yes, I am).

name: Subject pronouns
description: I, you, he, she, it, we, they: he for a man, she for a woman, it for a thing.

name: a / an
description: Use a or an before a singular countable noun; an before a vowel sound.

name: Plural nouns
description: Add -s or -es for more than one; some plurals are irregular (children, people).

name: my, your, his, her, our, their
description: Show who something belongs to: my, your, his, her, its, our, their.

name: Talking about age
description: Use be with years old, and ask with How old …?

name: the
description: Use the when the listener knows which one, or when there is only one.

name: this / that / these / those
description: this and these for things near you, that and those for things further away.

name: there is / there are
description: Say that something exists or is in a place; there is for one, there are for many.
examples: There is a bank near here.
There are two cafés on this street.

name: have got / has got
description: Talk about possessions and family; has got for he, she and it.
examples: She has got a new car.

name: Present simple: positive
description: Habits and facts; add -s or -es to the verb for he, she and it.

name: Present simple: negative
description: don't or doesn't before the base verb; the verb has no -s after doesn't.

name: Present simple: questions
description: Do or does before the subject, then the base verb.

name: can / can't
description: Ability and permission: can plus the base verb, the same for every person.

name: Imperatives
description: Give instructions with the base verb; use Don't for a negative.

name: Possessive 's
description: Add 's to a person to show that something belongs to them.

name: Prepositions of place
description: in (inside), on (on a surface), at (a point), next to, under, between.
examples: The keys are on the table.
The bank is next to the park.

name: in / on / at for time
description: at for clock times, on for days and dates, in for months, years and parts of the day.
examples: The film starts at seven o'clock.
I get up early in the morning.

name: Wh- questions
description: what, where, when, who, why and how start the question.

name: Present continuous: now
description: am/is/are plus the -ing form for actions happening now.
examples: She is talking on the phone.

name: like / love / hate + -ing
description: After like, love, enjoy and hate, use the -ing form of the verb.

name: would like
description: A polite way to ask for or offer something: would like plus a noun or to plus a verb.
examples: I'd like to pay by card.

name: Past simple: was / were
description: was for I, he, she and it; were for you, we and they.

name: Past simple: regular verbs
description: Add -ed to the verb for finished actions in the past.

name: Past simple: irregular verbs
description: Common verbs have their own past forms: go-went, have-had, see-saw.

name: Past simple: negatives and questions
description: didn't or did plus the base verb, never the past form.

name: be going to
description: Plans and intentions: am/is/are going to plus the base verb.
examples: I'm going to visit my parents.
We're going to buy a car.

name: will
description: Predictions, and decisions made at the moment of speaking.

name: Comparatives
description: -er or more plus than to compare two things; good-better, bad-worse.
examples: My car is older than yours.

name: Superlatives
description: the -est or the most for the top of a group; good-best, bad-worst.
examples: It's the biggest city in Turkey.
She is the most famous singer here.
This is the best day of my life.

name: some / any, much / many, a lot of
description: some in positive sentences, any in negatives and questions; many with countable nouns, much with uncountable ones.
examples: There is some milk in the fridge.

name: Adverbs of frequency
description: always, usually, often, sometimes and never go before the main verb and after be.
examples: I usually get up at seven.

name: have to / must / should
description: have to and must for obligation; should for advice.
examples: You must wear a seat belt.

name: Present simple or present continuous
description: Present simple for habits and facts, present continuous for what is happening now.
examples: I usually walk to work, but today I'm taking the bus.
What do you do? I'm a nurse.
What are you doing? I'm reading.

name: Object pronouns
description: me, you, him, her, it, us and them after verbs and prepositions.

name: and, but, because, so
description: Join ideas: and adds, but contrasts, because gives a reason, so gives a result.
examples: I was tired, so I went to bed.
I like tea, but I don't like coffee.

name: Present perfect: experience
description: have/has plus the past participle for life experience, often with ever and never.
examples: Have you ever been to London?

name: Verb + to or -ing
description: Some verbs take to plus a verb (want, need, decide); others take the -ing form (enjoy, finish).
